summary:
We've developed an interactive educational website that depicts how Earth's terrain changes over time, it focusing on three regions: Europe, Nepal, and the Amazon. Using NISAR satellite imagery, false-color radar composites, maps, and 3D models, our website allows the users to explore environmental changes such as flooding, deforestation, vegetation loss, and mountain instability around the world. The visitors of the site can select specific areas, examine the different radar polarization options (HV/HH), and also compare changes across different timeframes to better understand how Earth's surface evolves over the course of history. 

Our project not only addresses the challenge of having complex satellite data accessible and understandable to the general public, also can help educate and spread awareness about the changes our planet is going through. By transforming scientific imagery into interactive visualizations and integrating an AI chatbot featuring Steamboat Willie, we've made environmental information easier to explore and interpret. Our goal is to raise awareness of environmental changes, help communities recognize potential disaster warning signs, and encourage better preparedness that could ultimately save lives from being lost.
details:
We've developed a website that demonstrates how the terrain changes over time. We have different tabs that focus on Europe, Nepal, and the Amazon. Natural occurrences such as heatwaves, floods, and forest loss are depicted through the changing of imagery, including 3D models. Clicking on the area tabs gives you additional options on which change you want to focus on, such as HV/HH and flooding. You could choose to view the areas as maps or 3D models. Looking at the timeframe, you can see how the vegetation has changed over time. Darker areas represent smoother areas such as water while whiter area show cities.

Our intended impact on the project is to educate the general public and to spread awareness about how the earth changes over time. The website takes satellite images and makes it understandable for the public. This would allow for them to see the warning signs of disaster to better prepare. Hopefully, they could evacuate to safety early and prevent further future deaths.

Our exceptional coders used HTML5, CSS3 and plain JavaScript (ES6+) to develop our educational website. To further enhance our creativity, we formulated an AI chatbot-who's the cartoon character Steamboat Willie-that helps guide the viewer on what they are looking at and explains certain terminology written in the website.

We considered different factors such as using NISAR imagery to showcase the instability of the mountains, the changes in elevation, and how the flood scars the terrain of the area by using false-color radar composites to represent the surface structure, polarization, and/or land-cover changes.
